title: CMake, ABIs, Native Memory, and Rust Interoperability Check

questions.prompt: Which approach best applies cmake, abis, native memory, and rust interoperability?
options: Use target-scoped cross-compilation and a narrow C ABI with one explicit owner and allocator for every object and buffer.
Build all ABIs in one directory
questions.answer: Use target-scoped cross-compilation and a narrow C ABI with one explicit owner and allocator for every object and buffer.
questions.explanation: The correct response preserves authority, compatibility, exact artifact evidence, adverse-path behavior, and operational ownership.

questions.prompt: Rust removes all memory and concurrency risk from native Android code, including unsafe FFI boundaries.
questions.explanation: Passing a Rust-owned allocation to C++ free or a C++ allocation to Rust deallocation crosses allocator contracts and can corrupt memory.

questions.prompt: Why prefer a C ABI at a Rust interoperability boundary?
questions.answer: It provides a smaller, more stable and language-neutral calling contract than compiler-specific C++ ABI details.
questions.explanation: The answer identifies the contract or mechanism that remains valid beyond one implementation demonstration.
